title: Cardiologist visit
what: The doctor asks how you feel, listens to your heart, and checks your blood pressure. If needed, an ECG, heart ultrasound, or other tests are ordered.
why: For chest pain, shortness of breath, an irregular heartbeat, high blood pressure, swollen legs, or a check before surgery.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes; you get advice right away
tell_doctor: What bothers you, when, and with how much effort
Your blood pressure readings, if you check at home

prepare.title: Blood pressure diary
prepare.text: If you have a monitor, record your blood pressure morning and evening for 3 to 7 days.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take them as usual. Do not stop them on your own before the visit.

prepare.title: Before the visit
prepare.text: No strong coffee or smoking for an hour before. They change your blood pressure and pulse.

bring: A list of your medicines, or the packs themselves
Past ECGs, heart ultrasounds, and test results
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms and health
Your blood pressure and pulse are checked
The doctor listens to your heart and lungs
Your legs are checked for swelling
An ECG is often done right at the visit
The doctor explains the next steps
after: Have the tests your doctor ordered
Take your medicines as your doctor prescribed
Come back for a follow-up with the results
red_flags: Severe pressing chest pain lasting more than 15 minutes: call emergency services
Sudden severe shortness of breath or fainting: call emergency services

faq.a: Usually not. But if you have blood tests the same day, check with the clinic.

faq.q: Should I take my blood pressure pills that morning?
faq.a: Yes, as usual, unless your doctor says otherwise. That way the doctor sees how the treatment works.

reminders.text: Cardiologist visit tomorrow. Bring your medicine list, past ECGs, and blood pressure diary.
